validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed independently of GEM. FERC Docket CP20-27-000 (Federal Register notice 2020-01-07; FERC's own Sept-2020 Environmental Assessment, cms.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-09/cp20-27-000_EA_final_0.pdf) describes North Baja Pipeline LLC's Dec-16-2019 application to build the North Baja XPress Project: a new 31,900-ISO-hp Titan 250 compressor unit at the existing Ehrenberg Compressor Station (La Paz County, AZ) plus modifications to the El Paso Meter Station (La Paz County, AZ) and Ogilby Meter Station (Imperial County, CA). FERC's clarifying order (Reuters wire, reprinted by pgjonline.com 2023-05-30 and worldpipelines.com 2023-06-01 -- same wire story, counted once) confirms the expansion was put into full service by May 2023. EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects dataset (Historical Projects tab, row 1085, last updated 2023-07-06) independently lists this exact project (Docket CP20-27, Status=Completed, Completed Date 2023-05-25) -- a second, independent origin from the FERC docket/Reuters wire. Real project, not a GEM-only entity. CLASSIFICATION: correctly an interstate natural-gas transmission capacity expansion (FERC Authority=Interstate per EIA), not a gathering/process line; Fuel=Gas is trivially correct. DUPLICATE: NOT a duplicate of P0226 (the North Baja mainline). P2569/NBXP is a distinct FERC certificate (CP20-27) adding compression-only incremental capacity on the existing P0226 route -- GEM's segment-vs-project convention of a separate row for the expansion phase is correct and matches how EIA and FERC themselves track it (a separate docket/project entry layered on the existing pipeline). LengthKnown=0 / Diameter=blank on P2569 are CORRECT per the 'expansion with no new physical pipe' rule -- the FERC EA describes only compressor-unit and meter-station modifications, no new pipeline segment, and EIA's own Miles field for this project is blank/None. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1='North Baja Pipeline LLC' [100%] confirmed by TC Energy's own asset page (tcenergy.com/operations/natural-gas/north-baja-pipeline-system/, live, verified) and by the FERC docket, which names 'North Baja Pipeline, LLC ("North Baja")' as the certificate applicant/holder -- a second, independent corroboration comes from en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Baja_Pipeline, which places the asset under the TC Energy corporate family (though its 'TC PipeLines LP' parent reference looks stale post-2021 rollup -- that's a P0226-level ownership-chain question, not a P2569 defect). MINOR SCHEMA CAVEAT (not a fix, just a flag): the Location unit is marked 'irregular' in the worklist because 'Ogilby' sits under EndPrefecture/District while EndLocation and StartPrefecture/District are blank -- FERC's docket gives the county-level detail (La Paz County AZ start / Imperial County CA end) that would properly fill those blanks, but this looks like a data-entry convention shared with the parent row P0226 rather than a P2569-specific error, so I'm flagging rather than restaging the whole Location block. DELAY: Delayed=yes/DelayType=inferred is defensible and probably UNDERSTATED -- FERC's own 2020 EA states North Baja's ORIGINAL proposed schedule was construction starting Oct 2021 for an in-service date of Nov 1, 2022; the actual in-service (FERC order effective May 25/30, 2023, EIA Completed Date 2023-05-25) is about 6 months later than that stated target. That's a documented schedule slip against the applicant's own stated plan, not just an inference from silence -- a reviewer could reasonably upgrade DelayType to 'confirmed', though I'm leaving the existing lowercase-vocab value alone since no source uses the word 'delay' explicitly. Read all 6 of this row's harvested wiki citations plus the FERC EA and Federal Register notice (8 documents total); could not read northbajapipeline.com/company_info/ or tcplus.com/North%20Baja (both TC-affiliate mirror pages, same origin as tcenergy.com, low incremental value) or the dead-looking pre-2018 TransCanada citations -- didn't chase further since tcenergy.com/EIA/FERC already independently corroborate everything they'd support.

validity.recommendation: correct Capacity from 450 MMcf/d to 495 MMcf/d
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's Capacity=450.00 MMcf/d does NOT survive verification -- it is a stale figure. THREE independent origins all state 495, not 450: (1) FERC's own Sept-2020 Environmental Assessment for Docket CP20-27 states explicitly, in its own words: '495,000 dekatherms per day (495 million cubic feet per day) of incremental firm delivery capacity' (cms.ferc.gov EA PDF, p.1 and p.9 of the extracted text) -- this is the primary regulatory document, and the SAME 495,000-Dth/d figure already appears in the Dec-2019 Federal Register notice of application, i.e. the project was proposed at 495, not 450, from day one. (2) EIA's own Natural Gas Pipeline Projects dataset -- the SAME dataset GEM's wiki cites as its source for 450 -- has been updated since GEM last pulled it: the current file (eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects.xlsx, row 1085 of the Historical Projects tab, Last Updated Date 2023-07-06) now reads 'Additional Capacity (MMcf/d) = 495', not 450. GEM's own wiki page footnotes the 450 figure to an EIA access dated July 2020 -- i.e. a since-superseded EIA snapshot from before the project was finalized. (3) Reuters' wire story on FERC's May-2023 in-service order (reprinted by pgjonline.com and worldpipelines.com) states '495 MMcf/d' / '0.495 billion ft3/d' throughout. So: FERC docket (2019 AND 2020) + the current EIA dataset + the Reuters wire on the completed project all agree on 495; nothing corroborates 450 except a superseded EIA snapshot from mid-project. Capacity should be corrected to 495.00 MMcf/d; CapacityUnits (MMcf/d) is unchanged.
